path: Parent Vesion- Final Approved 7-15-2020_ Marsing School District 2020-21 Reopening Plan.docx
text: The Marsing School District is planning to begin school as planned on August 12, 2020 with all students on campus; however, families need to be aware that situations may develop which could impact those plans. As we continue to plan for school in the fall, we are considering all the possible scenarios and what steps we need to take to be prepared to offer the best educational services for our students. In our planning, we have focused on three potential scenarios for the fall: Scenario 1: Normal/Traditional- There is no community spread of COVID. All restrictions have been lifted, and schools can operate as normal. Scenario 2: Minor to moderate community spread of COVID and restrictions regarding physical distancing, health monitoring, and sanitation are in place. Schools could be closed temporarily and then reopen if a member of the school community has a confirmed case of COVID. Scenario 3: Widespread transmission of COVID. Schools are closed (while still being allowed to deliver remote learning). All learning is done remotely via online instruction and/or paper packets. Marsing Possible Scenarios Plan To make each of these scenarios easy to remember and implement, each possibility has been assigned a color designation: Green – Normal School OperationsMinimal or moderate community transmission (as defined by Idaho Department of Health &Welfare) and no positive cases in a school Marsing School District plans to start the year with schools open assuming conditions are the same as they are currently. Secondary students will be assigned computer devices that will become a regular part of the learning process. Elementary students will be taught how to use computer devices as a supplementary to their learning process. Students and teachers will conduct teaching and learning in their classrooms. Students will be instructed how to learn remotely using multiple tools in case remote learning becomes necessary. Buses will run. School lunch services will be provided. Safety procedures will be in place to reduce the chance of the spread of illness in all scenarios: Personal Protective Equipment Establish and maintain hand hygiene stations in key locations in school buildings Mask/face shields recommended but not required for staff/students Identify an isolation/screening room in each school Classroom Staff and students trained in physical distancing, handwashing, respiratory etiquette and mask use to mitigate exposure Hand sanitizer and promotion of regular hand washing Regular sanitation of desks and other hard surfaces and frequently touched parts of school buildings using cleaner approved to kill the coronavirus Arrangement of desks to account for physical distancing Limit the use of shared materials and spaces Office Strategies and Other Non-Instructional Spaces Maintain six feet of distance when possible Regular sanitation of surfaces Hand sanitizer at all workstations Cafeteria Regular hot lunch menu will be available Lunch times staggered to reduce occupants in the cafeteria In addition to the cafeteria, alternative lunch locations will be available Offer options to eat outside Hand sanitizer at start of all serving lines Self-service of pre-packaged food items only Visitors Educational information will be posted about reducing the risk of spread of contagions No unscheduled visitors Limit visitors to parents and essential visitors on campus Lock exterior doors during school hours Develop parent pick-up and drop-off procedures at each school Gatherings Implement strategies at each school that discourage gatherings in areas such as the bus lane, restrooms, recess, hallways, lunch, before and after school Limit field trips, assemblies, and other large gatherings if physical distancing cannot be achieved Online School OptionFor families who do not feel comfortable sending their student to school, the Marsing SD will offer a full online option for students through Edgenuity. At the elementary level, students will be taught the same subjects and standards as are taught at a traditional school. Teachers will collect work and provide feedback. Assessments and assignments will be graded. Group discussions will be part of the school day. At the secondary level, students will be able to choose from a selection of the academic courses that are available at traditional middle and high schools. High school students will register for English, math, science, social studies, etc. and will have the option to register for Honors and Advanced Placement versions of these courses, which will be offered depending on student enrollment numbers. Students enrolled in Edgenuity will be able to earn a Marsing high school diploma. Students can also participate in sports and activities at their home high school. To register your interest in attending Marsing’s Virtual Option this fall, please contact the building Principal. Yellow – Alternate Day ScheduleModerate community transmission (as defined by Idaho Department of Health & Welfare) and positive case(s) with some risk of exposure in an individual school and/or within the District Marsing developed this contingency plan as an option to avoid complete school closure. The plan’s implementation will be determined by guidance from Southwest District Health and other Idaho governmental authorities that have jurisdiction over school operations. If physical distancing requirements become more stringent, schools may go to an alternating schedule with half the students attending one day and the other half of students attending on the alternating days that keeps families on the same school schedule. When not in school, students will use their issued computer device/packet materials to continue learning remotely. Marsing recognizes that this plan places an additional burden on families who will need to make accommodations for the days when their students are not in school. This scenario was developed to avoid a complete school closure in order to maintain regular contact between teachers and students. Red – School Buildings ClosedSubstantial community transmission (as defined by Idaho Department of Health & Welfare) and widespread positive case(s) with significant risk of exposure within a school and/or multiple schools If there is a state-wide or local order to close all schools or an individual school, learning will continue remotely. Secondary students will use their 1-1 internet enabled devices, the transition to remote learning will happen immediately. Students will interact with their peers and teachers using an internet-enabled device. Elementary students will be assigned educational packet materials with virtual check-ins with classroom teachers. Students will submit work and receive feedback. Assessments and grading will continue until schools can reopen. Athletics and Extracurricular ActivitiesMarsing works with the Idaho High School Athletic Association (IHSAA) and the Western Idaho Conference (WIC) to develop plans for activities and athletics in fall of the 2020-2021 school year. As additional information is available about fall activities, Marsing School District will provide that information to parents and students. Basic Health and Safety Measures Following these basic measures can help prevent the transmission of disease: Do not come to school if you have any COVID symptoms Fever of 100.4°F or higher Cough Sore throat Difficulty Breathing Diarrhea Nausea Wear a mask is encouraged but not required when on the school bus Wash hands or use hand sanitizer frequently Practice social distancing when possible (6 feet) Measures to Create a Safer School Environment At home before coming to school, parents/guardians are encouraged to take your child’s temperature. Children with a temperature of 100.4°F or higher need to stay home and wait until all of the symptoms are gone without medication for 72 hours. Allow time for frequent hand washing or use of hand sanitizer Place hand sanitizers in each classroom, at entrances, and in the cafeteria Open windows to ventilate classrooms and halls Store sufficient supplies to clean and disinfect the school Clean and disinfect school buildings, classrooms, and restrooms daily and surfaces that are touched by many people (handrails, doorknobs, etc.) several times per day Restrict campus access for anyone (includes family members) who has arrived from a foreign country in the last 14 days Restrict campus access for anyone who is living with a person under self-quarantine due to possible contact with a confirmed case Social Distancing Measures Designate and mark entrances to prevent crowding during morning drop-off Stagger dismissal at the end of the school day to prevent crowding Limit large group gatherings, such as assemblies, athletic competitions, and other events that create crowded conditions Place desks and chairs facing one direction and maximize the distance between them Teach and model social distancing and avoid unnecessary touching Affix stickers on the floor to encourage distancing while in line (e.g., cafeteria) Avoid group activities Refrain from activities that require sharing class materials School Bus Procedures School buses will be disinfected regularly, paying particular attention to surfaces that are touched frequently. Students should stand 6 feet apart when waiting for the bus. Students are not required but encouraged to wear a mask while on the school bus. Hand sanitizer will be available on every school bus. The bus roof vent and other windows will be used for ventilation when the weather permits. Procedures When a Student or Staff has Symptoms at School Students or staff with COVID symptoms during school hours will be taken to a special isolation room located in The HUB building to be isolated from others. Depending on the situation, the person may be sent home. Parents should inform the school if someone in their home has traveled abroad in the last 14 days, had close contact with a confirmed case, or has been diagnosed with COVID. They must keep their child at home in all of these situations. If students or staff have COVID symptoms and do not receive a COVID test they need to stay home for 14 days and be symptom free. Procedures When a Student or Staff has Symptoms at Home Students or staff with any COVID symptoms need to stay home and wait until all of the symptoms are gone without medication for 72 hours. If the student or staff develops a fever of 100.4°F or higher or has worsening symptoms, he/she should contact their healthcare provider. If students or staff have COVID symptoms and do not receive a COVID test they need to stay home for 14 days and be symptom free. Procedures For Returning to School After COVID Testing Or A Family Member Has Tested For COVID A-symptomatic students or staff must stay home and self-quarantine until they receive their test result. An image of your test result must be submitted to the Office A COVID positive patient must remain in quarantine until the health authority releases them from quarantine. A person who has travelled abroad or has had close contact (less than 6 feet distance for more than 15 minutes) with a confirmed COVID case must quarantine for 14 days or show documentation of a negative test. After a person receives a negative test result, students or staff that have no COVID symptoms need to stay home and wait until all of the symptoms are gone without medication for 72 hours.
